title: 面包板：孔底下的金属条
summary: 先故意插错一次，看看面包板里到底哪些孔是连着的。
description: 面包板的孔下面藏着金属条：同一列 a–e 相通、f–j 相通，上下边缘的电源轨整排相通。本课先把电阻插错，看它被金属条短路，再搭一个能点亮 LED 的完整回路。

cards.title: 先插错一次
text: 今天的规矩：**先动手，再讲道理。**
面包板上的孔看起来一模一样，但它们下面并不是各自独立的。下面三步搭一个“错”的电路，然后看看右边的**诊断**说了什么。

cards.title: 孔底下藏着金属条
text: - **一列五个孔 = 一条金属条。** a5、b5、c5、d5、e5 下面是同一片金属。插在这五个孔里的脚，就像焊在了一起。
- **中间的凹槽把每一列切成两段。** a–e 是一条，f–j 是另一条，所以 e5 和 f5 **不通**。
- **边上的长排是电源轨。** 红线那排（tp、bp）当 +，蓝线那排（tn、bn）当 −，一整排都是通的。上面的轨和下面的轨互相不通。
![](fig:strips)
刚才电阻的两只脚都在第 5 列，它们是**同一个点**。两端没有电压差，就没有电流流过——电阻被金属条**短路**了，等于没装。
![](fig:short)
**规则：一个元件的两只脚，必须插在两条不同的金属条上。**

cards.title: 挪好电阻，接成一个圈
text: 电流要走一个**完整的圈**：从电池 + 出发，穿过电阻和 LED，再回到电池 −。少一段，就一点电流都没有。

cards.title: 带走这三句话
text: - **同列 a–e 相通，f–j 相通，中间的凹槽把它们隔开。**
- **一个孔只插一只脚。** 想把两样东西连起来，就插进同一条金属条的不同孔，或者用跳线接两条金属条。
- **真实面包板的坑：** 有些长面包板的电源轨在中间是**断开的**（红线中间有一个小缺口），左右两半要用跳线接起来。第一次用一块新板子，先拿万用表量一下。
下一个：电源和 GND——电流从哪里来，又回到哪里去。

caption.text: 同一列 a–e 是一条金属条，f–j 是另一条，中间的凹槽把它们隔开（✗ 不通）。上下的 +、− 电源轨各自一整排相通。

i18n.en: In one column a–e is one metal strip and f–j another; the trench keeps them apart (✗ not joined). Each +/− power rail is joined along its whole length.

caption.text: 左：两只脚在同一条金属条上，电阻被短路；右：两只脚在两条不同的金属条上，电流才会穿过它。

i18n.en: Left: both legs on one strip, the resistor is shorted. Right: the legs on two different strips, so current has to pass through it.

en.title: The breadboard: strips under the holes
en.summary: Plug a part in the wrong way once and find out which holes are joined inside.
en.description: Under the holes of a breadboard are metal strips: a–e of a column are joined, f–j are joined, and each power rail is joined along its length. In this lesson you first plug a resistor in wrong and watch the strip short it out, then build a complete loop that lights an LED.
hints: Holes a–e in the same column are connected, so c9 and d9 are electrically the same point.
Current needs a complete loop: out of +, through the parts, back to −. If the LED stays dark, follow that loop and find where it's broken.

cards.title: Get it wrong on purpose
text: Today's rule: **do it first, explain it after.**
Every hole on a breadboard looks the same, but they are not separate underneath. In the next three steps you build a "wrong" circuit — then see what the **diagnostics** on the right say.

cards.title: Metal strips under the holes
text: - **Five holes in a column = one metal strip.** Under a5, b5, c5, d5 and e5 is one piece of metal. Leads plugged into those five holes are as good as soldered together.
- **The trench cuts every column in two.** a–e is one strip and f–j is another, so e5 and f5 are **not** connected.

- **The long rows along the edges are power rails.** The red-line row (tp, bp) is used as +, the blue-line row (tn, bn) as −, and each whole row is connected. The top rails and the bottom rails are not connected to each other.
![](fig:strips)
Both legs of your resistor were in column 5, so they were **the same point**. No voltage across it means no current through it — the strip **shorted it out**; it might as well not be there.
![](fig:short)
**Rule: a part's two legs must go into two different metal strips.**

cards.title: Move the resistor and close the loop
text: Current needs a **complete loop**: out of the battery +, through the resistor and the LED, back into the battery −. Leave out one piece and no current flows at all.

cards.title: Three things to take with you
text: - **a–e of a column are joined, f–j are joined, and the trench keeps them apart.**
- **One lead per hole.** To connect two things, plug them into different holes of the same strip, or join two strips with a jumper.

- **A real-board trap:** on some long breadboards the power rails are **split in the middle** (a gap in the red line); join the two halves with a jumper. On a new board, check with a multimeter first.
Next: power and GND — where the current comes from and where it goes back to.

steps: In the toolbar on the left pick **Battery** (9V by default). Click **`tp1`** for the red lead (+), then **`tn1`** for the black lead (−).
Pick **Jumper** and click **`tp5`**, then **`a5`**: this brings +9V from the rail to column 5. The five lit holes a5–e5 are all at +9V now.
Pick **Resistor** and put both legs in column 5: **`c5`** and **`e5`**. Now look at the **diagnostics** on the right: what do they say about this resistor?
Click the resistor and press **Delete**. Place it again with the Resistor tool at **`c5`** and **`c9`**, and in **Properties** on the right set it to **`470 Ω`**. It now spans columns 5 and 9.
Pick **LED** (red): the **long lead** (anode, +) goes in **`d9`**, in the same column as the resistor's second leg; the **short lead** (cathode, −) goes in **`d12`**.
Pick **Jumper** and click **`a12`** and **`tn12`**: the LED's cathode goes back to the − rail. The loop is closed — the LED should light up!
Hover over a hole without clicking: every hole connected to it lights up. Try **`c9`**, **`f9`** and **`tp20`**. Then press **Check my circuit** below and answer two quick questions.

measurements.ask: The resistor's second leg is in c9 and the LED's long lead is in d9. Do they need a jumper between them?
choices: No: c9 and d9 are on the same metal strip, so they are already one point
Yes: two holes always need a jumper between them
measurements.explain: The five holes a–e of a column share one metal strip; plugging in is enough.

measurements.ask: If the LED's long lead went into f9 (across the trench), would the LED still light?
choices: No: the trench splits column 9 into a–e and f–j, so f9 is not connected to c9
measurements.explain: The two sides of the trench are two different strips. To cross it, use a jumper (or, like a chip, put one row of pins on each side).

measurements.ask: 电阻的第二只脚在 c9，LED 的长脚在 d9。它们之间要不要再接一根跳线？
choices: 不用：c9 和 d9 在同一条金属条上，本来就是同一个点
要：两个孔之间必须用跳线连起来
measurements.explain: 同一列的 a–e 五个孔下面是同一条金属条，插进去就已经连上了。

measurements.ask: 如果把 LED 的长脚插在 f9（凹槽的另一边），LED 还会亮吗？
choices: 不会：凹槽把第 9 列切成了 a–e 和 f–j 两段，f9 和 c9 不通
measurements.explain: 凹槽两边是两条不同的金属条。想跨过凹槽，要用跳线（或者像芯片那样，两排脚各插一边）。

steps.text: 左边工具栏选**「电池」**（默认 9V）。先单击 **`tp1`** 放红线（+），再单击 **`tn1`** 放黑线（−）。
选**「跳线」**，单击 **`tp5`** 再单击 **`a5`**：把 +9V 从电源轨引到第 5 列。亮起来的 a5–e5 五个孔现在都是 +9V。
选**「电阻」**，两只脚都插在第 5 列：**`c5`** 和 **`e5`**。然后看右边的**诊断**：它说这个电阻怎么了？
单击选中电阻，按 **Delete** 删掉。再用「电阻」工具重新插：**`c5`** 和 **`c9`**，在右边**「属性」**里把阻值改成 **`470 Ω`**。现在它跨在第 5 列和第 9 列之间。
选**「LED」**（红色）：**长脚**（正极）插 **`d9`**，和电阻的第二只脚在同一列；**短脚**（负极）插 **`d12`**。
选**「跳线」**，单击 **`a12`** 和 **`tn12`**：LED 的负极回到 − 轨。圈接上了，LED 应该亮了！
鼠标停在一个孔上（不要点）：和它相通的孔会一起亮起来。试试 **`c9`**、**`f9`**、**`tp20`**。然后点下面的**「检查我的电路」**，回答两道小题。

hints: 同一列的 a–e 是相通的，所以 c9 和 d9 在电气上是同一个点。
电流必须走一个完整的圈：从 + 出发，经过元件，回到 −。LED 不亮时，顺着这个圈找断开的地方。
